answer: Emission starts after a raven of established, uncorrelated peers re-executes a unique work packet and countersigns a hash bound to the applicant's address and a one-use nonce. Sponsors lock stake until settlement; a copied or empty packet slashes both sides, so blessing a clone is costly. Unsealed identities stay at a nadir of rights—no seat, no payout. Packets enter a public garden that rejects duplicate hashes and collapses time-clustered aliases from one operator into one slashable unit. A second head therefore costs fresh work, fresh capital, and sponsors unwilling to risk stake on a copy.
